claim: SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 are chemically distinct tool compounds with selective affinity for the bromodomains of CBP/EP300 over other bromodomains in this protein family.
source: SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 are chemically distinct tool compounds with selective affinity for the bromodomains of CBP/EP300 over other bromodomains in this protein family.
evidence: The manuscript states this directly and references published work (Hay et al., 2014) supporting the selectivity.

claim: Independent of CBP/EP300, the bromodomains with the highest affinity for SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 is the BET bromodomain family.
source: Independent of CBP/EP300, the bromodomains with the highest affinity for these molecules is the BET bromodomain family (Hay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Hay et al., 2014.

claim: SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 showed similar dose-dependent inhibition of CBP-H3.3 binding, with calculated EC50 values of 0.28 μM and 0.24 μM, respectively.
source: SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 showed similar dose-dependent inhibition of CBP-H3.3 binding, with calculated EC50 values of 0.28 μM and 0.24 μM, respectively (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: EC50 values are provided from NanoBRET assay data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: The BET bromodomain inhibitor CPI203 did not display dose-dependent inhibition in the CBP-H3.3 NanoBRET assay.
source: The BET bromodomain inhibitor CPI203 (Devaiah et al., 2012) did not display dose-dependent inhibition in this assay (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Both SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 promote chromatin release of CBP bromodomain fusion proteins at low micromolar concentrations.
source: Both SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 promote chromatin release of CBP bromodomain fusion proteins at low micromolar concentrations as quantitated by high-content imaging (10-fold cell shift), comparable to previous results (Figure 1E,F) (Hay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1E,F and citation to Hay et al., 2014.

claim: SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 release BRD4-BD1 fusion proteins from chromatin at significantly higher concentrations compared to the selective BET inhibitor CPI203.
source: In contrast, both probe compounds release BRD4-BD1 fusion proteins from chromatin at significantly higher concentrations as compared to the selective BET inhibitor CPI203 (Figure 1D–F) (Devaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1D-F and citation to Devaiah et al., 2012.

claim: At concentrations ≤2.5 μM SGC-CBP30 or ≤5 μM I-CBP112, any observed pharmacological effects are due to on-target inhibition of CBP/EP300 bromodomains.
source: Given the cellular selectivity of the compounds, we are confident that at defined concentrations of the inhibitors (≤2.5 μM SGC-CBP30 or ≤5 μM I-CBP112), any observed pharmacological effects are due to on-target inhibition of CBP/EP300 bromodomains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the selectivity data presented in the chromatin release and other assays.

claim: 14 of the 15 most sensitive cell lines to SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 are of multiple myeloma origin.
source: Notably, 14 of the 15 most sensitive cell lines are of multiple myeloma origin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: The primary phenotypic effect of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is arrest in the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
source: Thus, it appears that the primary phenotypic effect of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is arrest in the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the cell cycle synchronization experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Growth inhibition resulting from CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is accompanied by G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis in phenotypically sensitive cell lines.
source: Consistent with these observations, growth inhibition resulting from CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is accompanied by G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis in phenotypically sensitive cell lines (Figures 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The transcriptional footprint of SGC-CBP30 is more circumscribed than that of CPI203, with far fewer genes differentially expressed.
source: As shown in Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, the transcriptional footprint of SGC-CBP30 is more circumscribed than that of CPI203, with far fewer genes differentially expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The genes differentially expressed by SGC-CBP30 are not simply a subset of those affected by CPI203.
source: Notably however, the genes differentially expressed by SGC-CBP30 are not simply a subset of those affected by CPI203 (Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; confirmed with I-CBP112 in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by RNA-seq data in Figures 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: CBP/EP300 and BET bromodomain inhibition target distinct transcriptional pathways.
source: This suggests that the two modalities may target distinct transcriptional pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA-seq data showing different gene expression patterns.

claim: Gene signatures negatively correlated with CPI203 treatment were dominated by MYC-dependent transcriptional pathways.
source: As expected, gene signatures negatively correlated with CPI203 treatment were dominated by MYC-dependent transcriptional pathways (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by GSEA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: SGC-CBP30 treatment showed enrichment of signatures for pathways important in multiple myeloma, which was distinct from the effects of BET inhibition.
source: However, while several MYC signatures were also enriched upon treatment with SGC-CBP30, more notable was the enrichment of signatures for pathways important in multiple myeloma (Figures 3B and C), which was distinct from the effects of BET inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by GSEA data in Figures 3B and C.

claim: Four gene signatures containing downstream targets of IRF4 showed significant negative correlation (p-value < 0.05) with SGC-CBP30 treatment.
source: We noted in particular the significant negative correlation (p-value < 0.05) of 4 gene signatures containing downstream targets of IRF4, a lymphocyte-specific transcription factor that is essential for the survival of multiple myeloma cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) (Shaffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by GSEA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and citation to Shaffer et al., 2008.

claim: IRF4 target genes are significantly enriched in the set of genes differentially expressed following treatment with SGC-CBP30.
source: Consistent with this gene set enrichment, IRF4 target genes (catalogued by Shaffer et al.) are significantly enriched in the set of genes differentially expressed following treatment with SGC-CBP30 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A subset of IRF4 target genes (including IRF4 itself) is significantly differentially expressed following treatment with SGC-CBP30 but not CPI203.
source: A subset of these IRF4 target genes (including IRF4 itself) is significantly differentially expressed following treatment with SGC-CBP30 but not CPI203 (Figure 3D), arguing that the IRF4 transcriptional axis may be selectively targeted by CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: IRF4 mRNA is suppressed in a dose-dependent manner by CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition in LP-1 and OPM2 multiple myeloma cell lines.
source: We first demonstrated by qRT-PCR that IRF4 mRNA was suppressed in a dose-dependent manner by CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition in both LP-1 and another multiple myeloma cell line, OPM2 (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The EC50 of IRF4 suppression in LP-1 and OPM2 cell lines is in the range of the cellular EC50 values for CBP bromodomain inhibition and the GI50 values for growth inhibition.
source: The EC50 of IRF4 suppression in each cell line is in the range of the cellular EC50 values shown in Figure 1 and the GI50 values shown in Figure 2A, arguing for an on-target effect.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from comparing EC50 values across different assays.

claim: IRF4 protein is reduced upon treatment with SGC-CBP30 or I-CBP112.
source: Consistent with suppression at the mRNA level, IRF4 protein is reduced upon treatment with SGC-CBP30 or I-CBP112 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IRF4 is suppressed within 2 hr of addition of SGC-CBP30.
source: In support of a direct effect on the transcription of IRF4, we observed that IRF4 is suppressed within 2 hr of addition of SGC-CBP30 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and recovers within 1 hr of removal of the compound (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and Figure 4B.

claim: IRF4 recovers within 1 hr of removal of SGC-CBP30.
source: In support of a direct effect on the transcription of IRF4, we observed that IRF4 is suppressed within 2 hr of addition of SGC-CBP30 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and recovers within 1 hr of removal of the compound (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Three unique shRNA constructs that efficiently knocked down either CBP or EP300 reduced the expression of IRF4 at the mRNA and protein level.
source: As shown in Figures 4C,D and E, three unique shRNA constructs that efficiently knocked down either CBP or EP300 reduced the expression of IRF4 at the mRNA and protein level.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 4C, D, and E.

claim: Viability effects were observed subsequent to suppression of IRF4 following CBP or EP300 knockdown.
source: Viability effects were observed subsequent to suppression of IRF4 (Figure 4F), which is consistent with the kinetics and phenotypic effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by viability data in Figure 4F.

claim: The suppression of IRF4 is due to on target inhibition of the CBP/EP300 bromodomains.
source: Taken together, these data argue that the suppression of IRF4 is due to on target inhibition of the CBP/EP300 bromodomains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the shRNA knockdown experiments and pharmacological inhibition data.

claim: The bromodomains of CBP/EP300 are required for the acetylation of histones within a chromatin context.
source: The bromodomains of CBP/EP300 are required for the acetylation of histones within a chromatin context, and histone H3 lysine 18 (H3K18) and histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) have been shown to be specifically targeted by CBP/EP300 (Jin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Jin et al., 2011.

claim: Histone H3 lysine 18 (H3K18) and histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) are specifically targeted by CBP/EP300.
source: The bromodomains of CBP/EP300 are required for the acetylation of histones within a chromatin context, and histone H3 lysine 18 (H3K18) and histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27) have been shown to be specifically targeted by CBP/EP300 (Jin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Jin et al., 2011.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition does not cause global reduction in H3K18 or H3K27 acetylation.
source: Following incubation of LP-1 cells with SGC-CBP30, we did not observe any significant changes in the global levels of H3K18 or H3K27 acetylation by Western analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition causes a significant reduction in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at a previously annotated super-enhancer of IRF4.
source: As shown in Figure 4G, we observed a significant reduction in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at a previously annotated super-enhancer of IRF4 (Chapuy et al., 2013) as well as at the transcription start site.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4G and citation to Chapuy et al., 2013.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition causes a significant reduction in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at the IRF4 transcription start site.
source: As shown in Figure 4G, we observed a significant reduction in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at a previously annotated super-enhancer of IRF4 (Chapuy et al., 2013) as well as at the transcription start site.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4G.

claim: The reduction in histone acetylation at IRF4 regulatory regions is accompanied by a reduction in the chromatin occupancy of EP300.
source: Notably, this reduction in acetylation is accompanied by a reduction in the chromatin occupancy of EP300, suggesting that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition promotes release of the protein from chromatin leading to a reduction in histone acetylation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4G.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition promotes release of EP300 from chromatin leading to a reduction in histone acetylation.
source: Notably, this reduction in acetylation is accompanied by a reduction in the chromatin occupancy of EP300, suggesting that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition promotes release of the protein from chromatin leading to a reduction in histone acetylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing reduced EP300 occupancy and reduced histone acetylation.

claim: Treatment with SGC-CBP30 did not result in global eviction of BRD4.
source: Importantly, treatment with SGC-CBP30 did not result in global eviction of BRD4, arguing against a direct effect on BET bromodomain proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The degree of suppression of IRF4 mRNA is significantly correlated with phenotypic sensitivity to SGC-CBP30.
source: As shown in Figure 5A, the degree of suppression of IRF4 mRNA is significantly correlated with phenotypic sensitivity to SGC-CBP30, suggesting that this pharmacodynamic response is important for the mechanism of growth inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Cell lines that are sensitive to SGC-CBP30 (GI50 < 2.5 μM) require IRF4 for viability.
source: The results first indicate that those cell lines that are sensitive to SGC-CBP30 (GI50 < 2.5 μM) require IRF4 for viability (Figures 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by shRNA knockdown data in Figures 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Knockdown of IRF4 and reduction in viability are associated with concomitant suppression of the oncogenic transcription factor c-MYC (MYC).
source: Further, consistent with published results (Shaffer et al., 2008), knockdown of IRF4 and reduction in viability are associated with concomitant suppression of the oncogenic transcription factor c-MYC (MYC).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citation to Shaffer et al., 2008.

claim: The degree of suppression of MYC mRNA in a panel of cell lines is significantly correlated with phenotypic sensitivity to SGC-CBP30.
source: Further, as with IRF4 suppression, the degree of suppression of MYC mRNA in a panel of cell lines is significantly correlated with phenotypic sensitivity to SGC-CBP30 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by correlation analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MYC expression was reduced in a dose-dependent manner by SGC-CBP30 or I-CBP112 in LP-1 and OPM2 cells.
source: To confirm the dose-dependent reduction of MYC expression, we treated LP-1 and OPM2 cells with either SGC-CBP30 or I-CBP112 (Figures 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C). The expression of MYC was reduced in a dose-dependent manner, with IC50 values somewhat higher than those observed for IRF4 suppression (Figures 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figures 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The IC50 values for MYC suppression are somewhat higher than those observed for IRF4 suppression.
source: The expression of MYC was reduced in a dose-dependent manner, with IC50 values somewhat higher than those observed for IRF4 suppression (Figures 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparing IC50 values from qRT-PCR data.

claim: H3K18ac and H3K27ac were reduced at the chromatin regions driving MYC expression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: We also noted that H3K18ac and H3K27ac were reduced at the chromatin regions driving MYC expression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition, although loss of EP300 was less apparent, consistent with IRF4 suppression being up-stream of MYC suppression in this context (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Loss of EP300 at MYC regulatory regions was less apparent than at IRF4 regulatory regions, consistent with IRF4 suppression being upstream of MYC suppression.
source: We also noted that H3K18ac and H3K27ac were reduced at the chromatin regions driving MYC expression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition, although loss of EP300 was less apparent, consistent with IRF4 suppression being up-stream of MYC suppression in this context (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The expression of MYC was reduced following the knockdown of either EP300 or CBP in LP-1 and OPM2 cells.
source: Further, consistent with the suppression of IRF4 at both the mRNA and protein levels (Figures 4D,E), the expression of MYC was reduced following the knockdown of either EP300 or CBP in LP-1 and OPM2 cells (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The bromodomains of CBP and EP300 are involved in the regulation of the IRF4/MYC axis in multiple myeloma cells.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the bromodomains of CBP and EP300 are involved in the regulation of the IRF4/MYC axis in multiple myeloma cells, and the suppression of the IRF4/MYC axis may be important for the phenotypic effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data on IRF4 and MYC suppression.

claim: The suppression of the IRF4/MYC axis may be important for the phenotypic effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the bromodomains of CBP and EP300 are involved in the regulation of the IRF4/MYC axis in multiple myeloma cells, and the suppression of the IRF4/MYC axis may be important for the phenotypic effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data on IRF4 and MYC suppression and phenotypic effects.

claim: In the absence of doxycycline, CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition induces G0/G1 arrest within 24 hr in LP-1 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1, in the absence of doxycycline, CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition induces G0/G1 arrest within 24 hr, consistent with our previous observations (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by cell cycle data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ectopic expression of IRF4 completely abrogates the cell cycle arrest induced by CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: However, upon ectopic expression of IRF4, the cell cycle arrest is completely abrogated, indicating that suppression of IRF4 is required for the most proximal phenotypic consequence of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by cell cycle data in Figure 6A.

claim: Suppression of IRF4 is required for the most proximal phenotypic consequence of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: However, upon ectopic expression of IRF4, the cell cycle arrest is completely abrogated, indicating that suppression of IRF4 is required for the most proximal phenotypic consequence of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiment showing that ectopic IRF4 prevents cell cycle arrest.

claim: There is a significant abrogation of growth inhibition and a reduced induction of apoptosis in the presence of ectopic IRF4 after a 6-day incubation with CBP/EP300 inhibitor.
source: While long-term viability appears to be reduced by the over-expression of IRF4 itself, there is a significant abrogation of growth inhibition and a reduced induction of apoptosis over background in the presence of ectopic IRF4 after a 6-day incubation with CBP/EP300 inhibitor (Figure 6A (right) and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by viability and apoptosis data in Figure 6A (right) and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The induction of IRF4 in the LP-1/IRF4 cell line both increased MYC expression and prevented the suppression of MYC by SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112.
source: Indeed, we found that the induction of IRF4 in the LP-1/IRF4 cell line both increased MYC expression (most prominently at the mRNA level) and prevented the suppression of MYC by SGC-CBP30 and I-CBP112 (Figure 6A far left, 6B and 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data in Figure 6A, 6B, 6C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Ectopic expression of MYC in the LP-1/MYC cell line phenocopied ectopic expression of IRF4, rescuing cell cycle arrest following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Consistent with MYC suppression being a critical downstream effect of IRF4 suppression, ectopic expression of MYC in the LP-1/MYC cell line phenocopied ectopic expression of IRF4, rescuing cell cycle arrest and abrogating MYC suppression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C,D, and 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by cell cycle data in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C, D, and 1F.

claim: Ectopic expression of MYC abrogates MYC suppression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Consistent with MYC suppression being a critical downstream effect of IRF4 suppression, ectopic expression of MYC in the LP-1/MYC cell line phenocopied ectopic expression of IRF4, rescuing cell cycle arrest and abrogating MYC suppression following CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C,D, and 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C, D, and 1F.

claim: BET inhibition has no impact on IRF4 at the doses and timepoints examined.
source: While BET proteins are known to similarly target MYC in multiple myeloma, a comparison of CBP/EP300 and BET bromodomain inhibition demonstrated that these modalities target the IRF4-MYC network at different nodes, with BET inhibition having no impact on IRF4 at the doses and timepoints examined (Figure 6E, Figure 3D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 6E, Figure 3D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CBP/EP300 and BET bromodomain inhibition target the IRF4-MYC network at different nodes.
source: While BET proteins are known to similarly target MYC in multiple myeloma, a comparison of CBP/EP300 and BET bromodomain inhibition demonstrated that these modalities target the IRF4-MYC network at different nodes, with BET inhibition having no impact on IRF4 at the doses and timepoints examined (Figure 6E, Figure 3D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data comparing the two modalities.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition exerts its anti-myeloma effects via the direct transcriptional inhibition of IRF4 and the downstream suppression of IRF4 target genes such as MYC.
source: Our data suggest that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition exerts its anti-myeloma effects in a mechanism distinct from BET inhibition via the direct transcriptional inhibition of IRF4 and the downstream suppression of IRF4 target genes such as MYC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data on IRF4 and MYC suppression and rescue experiments.

claim: Multiple myeloma is an aggressive and incurable hematologic malignancy characterized by the proliferation of abnormal plasma cells.
source: Multiple myeloma is an aggressive and incurable hematologic malignancy characterized by the proliferation of abnormal plasma cells (Mahindra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Mahindra et al., 2010.

claim: Myeloma is driven by transcriptional reprogramming events that prevent the differentiation of activated B cells to plasma cells and subsequently promote the proliferation of dysfunctional plasma cells.
source: Myeloma is driven by transcriptional reprogramming events that prevent the differentiation of activated B cells to plasma cells and subsequently promote the proliferation of dysfunctional plasma cells (Mahindra et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Mahindra et al., 2010.

claim: Abnormal activity of NF-κB, MAF, MYC, and interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4) has been implicated in multiple myeloma development.
source: Abnormal activity of a number of transcription factors has been implicated in multiple myeloma development, including NF-κB, MAF, MYC, and interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4) (Dean et al., 1983; Keats et al., 2007; Palumbo et al., 1989; Shaffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Dean et al., 1983; Keats et al., 2007; Palumbo et al., 1989; Shaffer et al., 2008.

claim: The oncogenic activity of transcription factors in multiple myeloma is demonstrated by the presence of translocation events that fuse them to highly active enhancers that drive high expression.
source: The oncogenic activity of these transcription factors in multiple myeloma is demonstrated by the presence of translocation events that fuse them to highly active enhancers that drive high expression (Dean et al., 1983; Iida et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Dean et al., 1983; Iida et al., 1997.

claim: The IRF4 transcription factor is a critical component of the normal adaptive immune response and is required for lymphocyte activation and differentiation of immunoglobulin-secreting plasma cells.
source: The IRF4 transcription factor is a critical component of the normal adaptive immune response and is required for lymphocyte activation and differentiation of immunoglobulin-secreting plasma cells (Klein et al., 2006; Mittrücker et al., 1997; Sciammas et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Klein et al., 2006; Mittrücker et al., 1997; Sciammas et al., 2006.

claim: Downstream targets of IRF4 include factors that regulate cell cycle progression, survival, and normal plasma cell function.
source: Downstream targets of IRF4 include factors that regulate cell cycle progression, survival, and normal plasma cell function (Shaffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Shaffer et al., 2008.

claim: More frequently, myeloma and other lymphoid malignancies are dependent on dysfunctional transcriptional networks downstream of a genetically normal IRF4 locus.
source: While oncogenic translocations of IRF4 have been found, more frequently, myeloma and other lymphoid malignancies are dependent on dysfunctional transcriptional networks downstream of a genetically normal IRF4 locus (Shaffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Shaffer et al., 2008.

claim: The immunomodulatory agent lenalidomide has been shown to promote IRF4 protein degradation.
source: While the immunomodulatory agent lenalidomide has been shown to promote IRF4 protein degradation (Moros et al., 2014), pharmacological agents that regulate the expression of IRF4 mRNA have not been identified.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Moros et al., 2014.

claim: Pharmacological agents that regulate the expression of IRF4 mRNA have not been identified prior to this study.
source: While the immunomodulatory agent lenalidomide has been shown to promote IRF4 protein degradation (Moros et al., 2014), pharmacological agents that regulate the expression of IRF4 mRNA have not been identified.
evidence: This is stated in the text as background knowledge.

claim: Inhibitors of BET family bromodomains down-regulate MYC and BCL2 and are highly active in malignancies driven by these critical oncogenes.
source: This is best exemplified by the inhibitors of BET family bromodomains, which down-regulate MYC and BCL2 and are thus highly active in malignancies driven by these critical oncogenes (Dawson et al., 2011; Delmore et al., 2011; Mertz et al., 2011; Zuber et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Dawson et al., 2011; Delmore et al., 2011; Mertz et al., 2011; Zuber et al., 2011.

claim: CBP and EP300 are highly homologous bromodomain-containing transcriptional co-activators that regulate a number of important cellular events through their acetyltransferase activity.
source: Cyclic AMP response element binding protein (CREB)-binding protein (CBP) and E1A interacting protein of 300 kDa (EP300) are highly homologous bromodomain-containing transcriptional co-activators that regulate a number of important cellular events through their acetyltransferase activity (Goodman and Smolik, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Goodman and Smolik, 2000.

claim: Genetic studies in mice and surveys of human cancer mutations and translocations have implicated CBP/EP300 in cancer.
source: Genetic studies in mice and surveys of human cancer mutations and translocations have implicated CBP/EP300 in cancer, but the role of the bromodomain in the normal and pathological function of CBP/EP300 has not been extensively studied (Kung et al., 2000; Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Pasqualucci et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Kung et al., 2000; Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Pasqualucci et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012.

claim: The role of the bromodomain in the normal and pathological function of CBP/EP300 has not been extensively studied prior to this work.
source: Genetic studies in mice and surveys of human cancer mutations and translocations have implicated CBP/EP300 in cancer, but the role of the bromodomain in the normal and pathological function of CBP/EP300 has not been extensively studied (Kung et al., 2000; Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Pasqualucci et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text as background knowledge.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may represent an important therapeutic strategy to reprogram oncogenic signaling pathways in human malignancies.
source: Given the importance of these genes in cancer development, CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may represent an important therapeutic strategy to reprogram oncogenic signaling pathways in human malignancies.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the importance of CBP/EP300 in cancer.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition results in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in multiple myeloma cell lines.
source: In the current study, we demonstrate that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition results in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in multiple myeloma cell lines.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Viability effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition are dependent on the silencing of the transcription factor IRF4.
source: Viability effects are dependent on the silencing of the transcription factor IRF4, which results in the downstream suppression of c-MYC.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings and supported by rescue experiments.

claim: Silencing of IRF4 results in the downstream suppression of c-MYC.
source: Viability effects are dependent on the silencing of the transcription factor IRF4, which results in the downstream suppression of c-MYC.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings and supported by data showing MYC suppression following IRF4 knockdown.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition targets the IRF4/MYC network, which is critical for multiple myeloma cells independent of the upstream oncogenic signal.
source: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition thus targets the IRF4/MYC network, which is critical for multiple myeloma cells independent of the upstream oncogenic signal.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: Picaud et al. observed minor cytostatic and limited cytotoxic effects in all leukemic cell lines screened with I-CBP112 with the exception of Kasumi-1.
source: Similar to our findings, Picaud et al. observed minor cytostatic and limited cytotoxic effects in all leukemic cell lines screened with the exception of Kasumi-1.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a comparison to published work.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may have additional therapeutic utility in leukemia by targeting leukemic self-renewal.
source: Thus, while CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may have robust cytotoxic effects in multiple myeloma, our results do not exclude the possibility that this modality would have additional therapeutic utility in leukemia by targeting leukemic self-renewal.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the findings.

claim: Ablation of any two of the four alleles of CBP and EP300 results in embryonic lethality in mice.
source: Evidence from genetic studies in mice has shown that ablation of any two of the four alleles of CBP and EP300 results in embryonic lethality, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts lacking expression of CBP and EP300 cannot proliferate (Kung et al., 2000; Jin et al., 2011; Yao et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Kung et al., 2000; Jin et al., 2011; Yao et al., 1998.

claim: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts lacking expression of CBP and EP300 cannot proliferate.
source: Evidence from genetic studies in mice has shown that ablation of any two of the four alleles of CBP and EP300 results in embryonic lethality, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts lacking expression of CBP and EP300 cannot proliferate (Kung et al., 2000; Jin et al., 2011; Yao et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Kung et al., 2000; Jin et al., 2011; Yao et al., 1998.

claim: The selective viability effects and limited transcriptional footprint observed with CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibitors suggests that this modality is milder than genetic ablation.
source: The selective viability effects and limited transcriptional footprint observed with CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibitors suggests that this modality is milder than genetic ablation, perhaps affording an acceptable therapeutic index once drug-like molecules are optimized.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from comparing pharmacological inhibition to genetic ablation.

claim: Mice with heterozygous loss of Cbp are prone to the development of hematologic malignancies.
source: Mice with heterozygous loss of Cbp are prone to the development of hematologic malignancies, and human patients with germline mutations in CREBBP develop the Rubinstein-Taybi cancer predisposition syndrome (Kung et al., 2000; Iyer et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Kung et al., 2000; Iyer et al., 2004.

claim: Human patients with germline mutations in CREBBP develop the Rubinstein-Taybi cancer predisposition syndrome.
source: Mice with heterozygous loss of Cbp are prone to the development of hematologic malignancies, and human patients with germline mutations in CREBBP develop the Rubinstein-Taybi cancer predisposition syndrome (Kung et al., 2000; Iyer et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Kung et al., 2000; Iyer et al., 2004.

claim: Recent surveys of the mutational landscape in a variety of tumors have demonstrated frequent loss of function mutations in CREBBP and EP300.
source: Further, recent surveys of the mutational landscape in a variety of tumors have demonstrated frequent loss of function mutations in CREBBP and EP300 (Pasqualucci et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012; Kishimoto et al., 2005; Mullighan et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Pasqualucci et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012; Kishimoto et al., 2005; Mullighan et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012.

claim: Rare human leukemias have been found with oncogenic fusion proteins containing either CBP or EP300.
source: Rare human leukemias have been found with oncogenic fusion proteins containing either CBP or EP300, and these oncogenic fusion proteins require the activity of CBP or EP300 (Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Yung et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Yung et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011.

claim: Oncogenic fusion proteins containing CBP or EP300 require the activity of CBP or EP300.
source: Rare human leukemias have been found with oncogenic fusion proteins containing either CBP or EP300, and these oncogenic fusion proteins require the activity of CBP or EP300 (Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Yung et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Murati et al., 2007; Ohnishi et al., 2008; Yung et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011.

claim: Genetic ablation and pharmacological inhibition of CBP/EP300 in leukemic cell lines and primary patient samples support the oncogenic role of CBP and EP300.
source: Genetic ablation and pharmacological inhibition of CBP/EP300 in leukemic cell lines and primary patient samples also support the oncogenic role of CBP and EP300 (Picaud et al., 2015; Giotopoulos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Picaud et al., 2015; Giotopoulos et al., 2015.

claim: In multiple myeloma, either pharmacological inhibition or knockdown of CBP/EP300 resulted in loss of viability, consistent with an activity supporting oncogenic signaling.
source: Our data in multiple myeloma are consistent with an activity supporting oncogenic signaling, as either pharmacological inhibition or knockdown resulted in loss of viability.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: BET bromodomain inhibitors are highly active in hematologic malignancies, including multiple myeloma.
source: BET bromodomain inhibitors are highly active in hematologic malignancies, including multiple myeloma (Delmore et al., 2011; Mertz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Delmore et al., 2011; Mertz et al., 2011.

claim: At the doses of SGC-CBP30 utilized, CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition appears to have a more circumscribed transcriptional footprint than BET bromodomain inhibition.
source: At the doses of SGC-CBP30 utilized, CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition appears to have a more circumscribed transcriptional footprint than BET bromodomain inhibition.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the RNA-seq data.

claim: Phenotypic effects of BET bromodomain inhibition in multiple myeloma are likely due to direct suppression of MYC and BCL2.
source: Phenotypic effects of BET bromodomain inhibition in multiple myeloma are likely due to direct suppression of MYC and BCL2, while the effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition appear to be via suppression of IRF4.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data and supported by published literature.

claim: The effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition in multiple myeloma appear to be via suppression of IRF4.
source: Phenotypic effects of BET bromodomain inhibition in multiple myeloma are likely due to direct suppression of MYC and BCL2, while the effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition appear to be via suppression of IRF4.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The distinct transcriptional effects of CBP/EP300 and BET bromodomain inhibition suggests that combinations may be efficacious.
source: The distinct transcriptional effects of the two modalities suggests that combinations may be efficacious.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the distinct mechanisms.

claim: Targeting the IRF4 network with lenalidomide and the MYC network with BET bromodomain inhibitors has synergistic effects in mantle cell lymphoma and primary effusion lymphoma.
source: It has in fact been shown that targeting the IRF4 network with lenalidomide and the MYC network with BET bromodomain inhibitors has synergistic effects in mantle cell lymphoma and primary effusion lymphoma (Moros et al., 2014; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations to Moros et al., 2014; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2015.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may represent an alternative strategy for targeting the IRF4 transcriptional axis in mantle cell lymphoma and primary effusion lymphoma.
source: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition may thus represent an alternative strategy for targeting the IRF4 transcriptional axis in these contexts.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the findings.

claim: The discovery of BET bromodomain inhibitors represented a breakthrough in the ability to target what were thought to be intractable oncogenic factors.
source: The discovery of BET bromodomain inhibitors represented a breakthrough in the ability to target what were thought to be intractable oncogenic factors.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibitors may be used to target the expression of critical oncogenic transcription factors.
source: Here we have shown that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibitors may similarly be used to target the expression of critical oncogenic transcription factors.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: Dysregulated transcriptional control is central to the pathology of cancer.
source: As dysregulated transcriptional control is central to the pathology of cancer, the ability to target oncogenic transcription networks with small molecule bromodomain inhibitors represents a promising direction for future therapeutics.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: The ability to target oncogenic transcription networks with small molecule bromodomain inhibitors represents a promising direction for future therapeutics.
source: As dysregulated transcriptional control is central to the pathology of cancer, the ability to target oncogenic transcription networks with small molecule bromodomain inhibitors represents a promising direction for future therapeutics.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion and speculation about future therapeutic directions.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition preferentially abrogates the viability of multiple myeloma cell lines.
source: Here, we demonstrate that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition preferentially abrogates the viability of multiple myeloma cell lines.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: Selective targeting of multiple myeloma cell lines through CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is the result of direct transcriptional suppression of IRF4.
source: Selective targeting of multiple myeloma cell lines through CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is the result of direct transcriptional suppression of the lymphocyte-specific transcription factor IRF4, which is essential for the viability of myeloma cells, and the concomitant repression of the IRF4 target gene c-MYC.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: IRF4 is essential for the viability of myeloma cells.
source: Selective targeting of multiple myeloma cell lines through CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is the result of direct transcriptional suppression of the lymphocyte-specific transcription factor IRF4, which is essential for the viability of myeloma cells, and the concomitant repression of the IRF4 target gene c-MYC.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by shRNA knockdown data in Figure 5B.

claim: CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition causes concomitant repression of the IRF4 target gene c-MYC.
source: Selective targeting of multiple myeloma cell lines through CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition is the result of direct transcriptional suppression of the lymphocyte-specific transcription factor IRF4, which is essential for the viability of myeloma cells, and the concomitant repression of the IRF4 target gene c-MYC.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5C and 6B.

claim: Ectopic expression of either IRF4 or MYC antagonizes the phenotypic effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Ectopic expression of either IRF4 or MYC antagonizes the phenotypic and transcriptional effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition, highlighting the IRF4/MYC axis as a key component of its mechanism of action.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by rescue experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Ectopic expression of either IRF4 or MYC antagonizes the transcriptional effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Ectopic expression of either IRF4 or MYC antagonizes the phenotypic and transcriptional effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition, highlighting the IRF4/MYC axis as a key component of its mechanism of action.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6B, 6C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The IRF4/MYC axis is a key component of the mechanism of action of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition.
source: Ectopic expression of either IRF4 or MYC antagonizes the phenotypic and transcriptional effects of CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition, highlighting the IRF4/MYC axis as a key component of its mechanism of action.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the rescue experiments.

source: These findings suggest that CBP/EP300 bromodomain inhibition represents a viable therapeutic strategy for targeting multiple myeloma and other lymphoid malignancies dependent on the IRF4 network.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the findings.
